hints: Look closely at the three dimensions of the last block, 5 x 10 x 15 mm, and compare its shortest side with the 5 x 5 x 5 mm cube. What is the same?
Remember that for complete diffusion, dye must reach the centre of the block, so the limiting distance is half of the shortest side, not the total volume.
walkthrough:
**Spot what really controls diffusion time**

Think like the dye molecule. It diffuses in from all surfaces at the same time. Complete diffusion is finished when it reaches the very centre.

So the key is not volume, it is the shortest distance from surface to centre.

**Calculate the distance to the centre**

For any block, distance to centre = shortest side / 2.

For 5 x 5 x 5 mm cube:
$$distance = 5 / 2 = 2.5 \text{ mm}$$
For 10 x 10 x 10 mm cube:
$$distance = 10 / 2 = 5.0 \text{ mm}$$
For 15 x 15 x 15 mm cube:
$$distance = 15 / 2 = 7.5 \text{ mm}$$
That is why time increases from 6.2 s to 16.1 s to 34.5 s.

**Apply this to the 5 x 10 x 15 mm block**

The shortest side is still 5 mm, even though the block is longer in the other directions.
$$distance = 5 / 2 = 2.5 \text{ mm}$$
This is identical to the 5 x 5 x 5 mm cube, so the predicted time is the same, 6.2 s.

options.A: Correct. The shortest diffusion distance to the centre is 2.5 mm, exactly the same as the 5 x 5 x 5 mm block, so time is 6.2 s.
options.B: Not correct. 16.1 s is for a 5.0 mm distance to centre in the 10 mm cube, which is twice as far as in this block.
options.C: Not correct. 34.5 s is for a 7.5 mm distance to centre in the 15 mm cube, much further than the 2.5 mm here.
options.D: Not correct. A larger volume does not mean longer time if the shortest side stays small, dye reaches the centre quickly from the close faces.
